Hello students, 

This thread exists to create pointers to concrete resources that can help students review material that they might be rusty on. Feel free to add your own helpful pointers here. Of course, this kind of reference material can just jog your memory --- the internalization of these concepts and skill in their use happened when you took the courses, did the homeworks, etc. 



Optimization and key linear-algebraic math: (EECS 127/227A stuff)

https://inst.eecs.berkeley.edu/~ee127/sp24/assets/notes/eecs127_reader.pdf

And from one of Prof. Sahai's past TAs in 189/289A:

http://gwthomas.github.io/docs/math4ml.pdf

This also has some probability in it.



Machine Learning: (189/289A stuff)

Jonathan Shewchuk's notes: http://www.cs.berkeley.edu/~jrs/papers/machlearn.pdf

Probability (EECS 126 stuff)

https://www.springer.com/us/book/9783030499945

As well as notes from:

https://inst.eecs.berkeley.edu/~ee126/sp25/
